entries.name: Financial Control
entries.MERGED_ENTRY: The author merged these tactics into ONE entry. Write a single entry under the name 'Financial Control' that fully covers every member below. In expanded_definition say the others are the same tactic under different names, and name them. Draw what_it_sounds_like, what_it_is_not and the other lists from ALL members (choose the best and most distinct items; do not just concatenate). Each member's previously written entry, if there is one, is the best starting text.

members.name: Financial Control
members.source_definition: Restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence.

existing_specific_text.short_definition: Restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence.
existing_specific_text.expanded_definition: Restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence. Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unsafe or unhappy situation. As a communication pattern, Financial Control-type behavior in the Control & Domination category tends to work by narrowing another person's practical options — money, movement, access — so compliance becomes the path of least resistance — describing a pattern in the exchange, not a fixed trait in the person.
existing_specific_text.plain_language_summary: In plain terms: restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence.
existing_specific_text.why_this_matters: Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unsafe or unhappy situation. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.
what_it_is: Restricting someone's access to money, financial information, earning capacity, or economic independence to enforce dependence.
Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unsafe or unhappy situation.
Contrasts with a healthier version: shared, transparent finances that both people can see and neither can unilaterally lock the other out of.
Recognizable by phrasing such as "You don't need your own bank account".
what_it_sounds_like: You don't need your own bank account.
I'll decide what you get to spend.
You don't need bank account.
I'll decide what you can spend.
You're not allowed to work.
what_it_is_not: Genuinely agreed household budgeting with one person tracking the books isn't control by itself — the flag is unilateral restriction imposed as leverage, not shared agreement.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Genuine, mutually agreed divisions of financial labor, with full transparency, are healthy and common.
common_false_positives: A genuine, mutual agreement about how shared finances are managed, that both people can see and access.
A temporary arrangement during a real financial hardship, openly discussed and not designed to be permanent or one-sided.
A person managing finances as an agreed division of labor, with full transparency and no restriction on the other's independent access.
discernment_questions: Does the target have real, independent access to money and financial information, or is it controlled entirely by one person?
Is any restriction mutually agreed and transparent, or unilaterally imposed?
Would the target be able to leave the relationship financially if they needed to?
Does financial management stay transparent, or is information specifically withheld from the target?
less_concerning_if: Financial arrangements are transparent, mutually agreed, and both people retain real independent access.
more_concerning_if: Money, information, or earning capacity is unilaterally restricted, leaving the target financially unable to act independently.
existing_specific_text.repair_check: After the incident, was there a genuine acknowledgment (not a non-apology), a concrete change in behavior, and no repeat of the same pattern? Repair is a pattern of change over time, not a single sentence of regret.
existing_specific_text.boundary_respect_check: When a boundary was stated plainly in this area, was it honored going forward — or tested, ignored, punished, or reframed as unreasonable? Boundary respect observed over multiple instances is one of the more reliable signals available.
existing_specific_text.psychological_mechanism: One documented mechanism behind patterns like this is that they can operate by narrowing another person's practical options — money, movement, access — so compliance becomes the path of least resistance. This describes a possible mechanism, not a claim about what any specific person intended.
existing_specific_text.possible_impact_on_receiver: People sometimes describe reduced practical independence and a narrowing sense of what options are actually available in connection with patterns like this. Impact varies widely by person, history, and context — this is a possibility to consider, not a predicted or universal outcome, and it is not a diagnosis of the person on the receiving end of a sustained pattern like this.
existing_specific_text.boundary_script: Given the safety dimension of this category, a scripted line matters less than the surrounding plan: if and when it feels safe, a simple, low-detail line like "I need some space and I'll reach out when I'm ready" is enough — it does not require justification. See the Safety note below before deciding how, when, or whether to address this directly with the person involved.
existing_specific_text.safety_note: A phrase-matching tool cannot decide safety. If this involves threats, monitoring, isolation, sex, money, housing, immigration, self-harm pressure, retaliation, or fear for safety, prioritize real-world support from a trusted person, local support service, legal/workplace resource, or emergency help if immediate danger exists.
misuse_warning: One example is a signal to examine, not proof of motive, diagnosis, abuse, danger, or character. Do not use this label to attack, shame, threaten, expose, or retaliate against someone.

members.name: Financial Enmeshment
members.source_definition: Using money and assets as an instrument of control.

existing_specific_text.short_definition: Using money and assets as an instrument of control.
existing_specific_text.expanded_definition: Using money and assets as an instrument of control. Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unhealthy situation. As a communication pattern, Financial Enmeshment-type behavior in the Control & Domination category tends to work by narrowing another person's practical options — money, movement, access — so compliance becomes the path of least resistance — describing a pattern in the exchange, not a fixed trait in the person. This entry also covers what earlier lists called: Financial Dependence-by-Design — combined here as one entry since they describe the same underlying pattern.
existing_specific_text.plain_language_summary: In plain terms: using money and assets as an instrument of control.
existing_specific_text.why_this_matters: Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unhealthy situation. Naming a pattern accurately — without over-claiming — is usually what restores clarity faster than either ignoring it or catastrophizing it.
what_it_is: Using money and assets as an instrument of control.
Financial control is one of the strongest practical barriers to leaving an unhealthy situation.
Contrasts with a healthier version: transparent shared budgeting both people can see and veto.
Recognizable by phrasing such as "My money, my rules".
Also covers the related, previously separate entries: Financial Dependence-by-Design.
what_it_sounds_like: My money, my rules.
You'll get your allowance when you behave.
My house, my rules.
I'll cut you off your card.
Everything here is in my name.
You'll get your allowance when I say.
Ask me for permission before you spend.
what_it_is_not: Households genuinely do have one earner and shared rules — the flag is money framed as leverage over behavior, not budgeting.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Genuine, long-term financial interdependence is normal in many committed relationships.
common_false_positives: A genuine, transparent shared budget that both people can see and have real input into.
Real financial interdependence built through a mutual, long relationship, that isn't used as leverage in disagreements.
A household with intertwined finances by necessity, where both people retain meaningful, if imperfect, financial agency.
discernment_questions: Can the target see and meaningfully weigh in on shared financial decisions, or is access one-sided?
Is intertwined finance used as leverage during disagreements, or does it stay separate from conflict?
Would the target retain some financial agency even in a disagreement?
Does "my money, my rules" reflect actual unilateral control, or shorthand within a genuinely mutual system?
less_concerning_if: Shared finances are transparent and both people retain meaningful input and agency.
more_concerning_if: Financial intertwinement is unilaterally controlled and specifically invoked as leverage during disagreements.
